info.name: Lecture 2 - Products
info.description:
# E-commerce Training API — Lecture 2: Products

This collection covers the **Products module**: browsing/searching the public catalog, and the admin-only Create/Update/Delete endpoints.

## How to use this collection
1. Set the `baseUrl` collection variable if your backend isn't running at the default `http://localhost:5000/api` (Collection → Variables tab).
2. Make sure the backend is running (`npm run dev`) and seeded (`npm run seed` — this creates the admin/test users **and** at least 14 sample products across 4 categories).
3. Browse the public requests in the **Lecture 2 - Products** folder freely — `Get All Products`, `Search Products`, `Filter by Category`, `Filter by Price Range`, `Sort Products`, `Paginate Products`, `Featured Products Only`, `Get Categories List`, and `Get Product By ID` all work with no login.
4. Before trying **Create Product**, **Update Product**, or **Delete Product**, run **Setup → Admin Login (get token)** once. Its Tests tab automatically saves the returned JWT into the `{{token}}` collection variable, which those requests already send as `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}`.
5. Need to upload actual image files from your computer instead of pasting URLs? Use **Create Product - Upload From Device (Admin)** — same endpoint, `multipart/form-data` body instead of JSON.

## Response shape
Every endpoint in this API replies with one of two shapes:

```jsonc
// success
{ "success": true, "data": { ... } }

// error
{ "success": false, "message": "Human readable message", "errors": [] }
```

`errors` is populated (an array of `{ field, message }`) when the failure came from input validation; otherwise it's an empty array.

## Note
This collection only covers Products. For Register/Login/Me/Logout, import the separate **Lecture 1 - Authentication** collection.

request.description:
Logs in as the seeded admin account and grabs a JWT you can use for the **admin-only** requests in this collection: **Create Product**, **Update Product**, and **Delete Product**.

**Run this once before touching those three requests.** Its Tests tab automatically copies the token from the response into the `{{token}}` collection variable, so every admin request below sends `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}` for you — nothing to copy/paste.

This is the exact same `/api/auth/login` endpoint covered in the Lecture 1 - Authentication collection; it's duplicated here (with the admin credentials pre-filled) so this Products collection works standalone even if you haven't imported Lecture 1.

**Good to know:**
- The seeded admin is `admin@test.com` / `Admin123` (created by `npm run seed` on the backend).
- A normal (non-admin) account can log in fine here too, but its token will get a `403 Forbidden` on Create/Update/Delete — see those requests' saved error examples.

response.name: Success - Logged in as admin
Error - Wrong credentials

request.description:
Returns a **paginated** list of products. This is the request your product listing / home page grid would call with no filters applied.

**Defaults when you send no query params:** `page=1`, `limit=10`, sorted newest-first.

**Response shape:**
```jsonc
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "products": [ ... up to `limit` items ... ],
    "page": 1,
    "totalPages": 2,
    "totalProducts": 14
  }
}
```
Use `page` + `totalPages` to build pager buttons, and `totalProducts` for a "showing X of Y results" label.

**This route is public** — no `Authorization` header needed, and every combinable filter is optional. See the other requests in this folder (**Search**, **Filter by Category**, **Filter by Price Range**, **Sort**, **Paginate**, **Featured Only**) for how to use each query param — they all hit this exact same endpoint, just with different query strings.

**Good to know:** this endpoint never returns an error response — unrecognized or malformed query params are simply ignored and it falls back to defaults, so there's no saved error example here (unlike the other 5 endpoints in this collection).

request.description:
Full-text search across a product's `name` and `description` fields, using MongoDB's `$text` index (fast — not a slow regex scan).

**Query param:** `search` — try `headphones`, `coffee`, `yoga`, etc.

Combine it with any other filter, e.g. `?search=shoes&category=Clothing`.

**Good to know:** if nothing matches, you still get a normal `200` response with an empty `products` array and `totalProducts: 0` — that's not an error, it's just "no results" (see the second saved example).

request.description:
Filters products whose `price` falls within a range.

**Query params (both optional, independent):**
- `minPrice` — only products priced at or above this
- `maxPrice` — only products priced at or below this

Send just one of them for an open-ended range (e.g. `?minPrice=100` = "$100 and up"), or both for a bounded range like the example here (`$50–$150`).

request.description:
Controls the sort order of results.

**Query param `sort`, one of:**
- `price_asc` — cheapest first
- `price_desc` — most expensive first
- `newest` — most recently added first (this is also the **default** when `sort` is omitted)
- `rating` — highest rated first

Any other/unrecognized value silently falls back to `newest`.

request.description:
Controls which "page" of results comes back.

**Query params:**
- `page` — defaults to `1`
- `limit` — items per page, defaults to `10` (capped at `100` server-side so a typo can't accidentally ask for the entire catalog)

This example asks for page 2 with 5 items per page — i.e. products 6-10 out of the total.

Read `data.page` / `data.totalPages` / `data.totalProducts` from the response to build "Page 2 of 3" style pagination controls.

request.description:
Returns only products marked `isFeatured: true` — this is what feeds the "Featured" section on the home page.

**Query param:** `featured=true`.

**Good to know:** the check is strictly `featured === "true"`. Sending `featured=false`, `featured=0`, or anything else does **not** filter out featured products — it's simply treated as "not set" and you get the full unfiltered list back. If you want "only non-featured", you'd need to filter that client-side (there's no server param for it in this lecture).

request.description:
Returns the list of **distinct** category names currently in use across all products — exactly what you need to build the category filter dropdown or the home page's category tiles, without hardcoding category names in the frontend.

**What you get back:** a plain array of strings, not an array of objects.

**Good to know:**
- This is a **public** route — no token needed.
- There's no error case for this endpoint: if there happen to be zero products in the database, it just returns `"data": []`, still with `"success": true`.

response.name: Success - Category list

request.description:
Returns a single product — this is the request behind a Product Details page.

**What to send:** the Mongo `id` in the URL path (copy it from any product object returned by the other requests in this folder).

**Good to know:**
- This is a **public** route — no token needed.
- If the `id` is a validly-formatted Mongo ObjectId but doesn't match any product, you get a clean `404` (see the saved error example) — this is the case you should handle on the frontend with a "Product not found" page.
- If the `id` isn't even a valid ObjectId format (e.g. you pasted a slug or a random string), you instead get a generic `400 Invalid _id` from the shared error handler.

request.description:
Creates a new product. This is what the admin dashboard's "Add Product" form submits to.

**Required fields:** `name`, `description`, `price` (must be ≥ 0), `image`, `category`.
**Optional fields:** `images` (array, defaults to `[]`), `brand`, `countInStock` (defaults to `0`, must be ≥ 0), `isFeatured` (defaults to `false`).

**What you get back:** the created product, including its server-generated `id` and `slug` (auto-derived from `name` — you never send `slug` yourself).

**This is an admin-only route:**
1. Run **Setup → Admin Login (get token)** first so `{{token}}` holds a valid admin JWT.
2. This request already sends `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}` (see the Authorization tab) — nothing else to configure.

**Good to know:**
- A logged-in user whose role is `"user"` (not `"admin"`) gets a `403 Forbidden` here — see the saved error example. That's different from a `401`: `403` means "I know who you are, you're just not allowed."
- Missing/invalid fields return a `400` with a per-field `errors` array — also saved as an example below.

response.name: Success - Product created

body.raw:
{
  "name": "Ceramic Pour-Over Coffee Dripper",
  "description": "A hand-glazed ceramic pour-over dripper that fits most standard mug sizes, for a cleaner cup than drip machines.",
  "price": 22.5,
  "image": "https://picsum.photos/seed/pourover/600/600",
  "images": [
    "https://picsum.photos/seed/pourover-2/600/600"

request.description: Same endpoint as **Create Product (Admin)**, but sends actual image files from your device instead of image URLs. **What to send:** `multipart/form-data` (select this request's Body tab → `form-data`, already configured below): - Text fields: `name`, `description`, `price`, `category`, `brand`, `countInStock`, `isFeatured` — identical to the JSON version. - File fields: `image` (pick 1 file — this becomes the main image) and `images` (you can attach up to 5 files — the gallery). Click the `image`/`images` row, switch its type to "File" if it isn't already, then click "Select Files". **What you get back:** the created product. `image`/`images` in the response are server paths like `/uploads/products/.jpg` — prefix them with your backend origin (e.g. `http://localhost:5000`) to load them in a browser/`` tag; `{{baseUrl}}` already includes `/api`, so don't reuse it for the image URL. **Good to know:** - **Admin-only**, same as the JSON version: `403` for a non-admin token. - Only `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/webp`, `image/gif` are accepted; anything else is rejected with `400`. - Each file is capped at 5MB. - You can mix modes across requests (some products via URL, others via upload) — the backend stores whichever `image`/`images` value it ends up with the same way either way.

Updates an existing product. This is what the admin dashboard's "Edit Product" form submits to.

**What to send:** only the fields you want to change (this is a partial update, like the example body here which just adjusts `price`, `countInStock`, and `isFeatured`) — you don't have to resend the entire product. Any of the same fields accepted by **Create Product** can be updated.

**Good to know:**
- **Admin-only**, same as Create: needs `{{token}}` to be an admin JWT (run **Setup → Admin Login** first), otherwise `403`.
- If you change `name`, the `slug` is automatically regenerated to match.
- If the `id` in the URL doesn't match any product, you get a `404` — see the saved error example.

request.description:
Permanently deletes a product. This is what the admin dashboard's "Delete" button calls — there's no soft-delete/undo in this lecture, so treat it as irreversible.

**What to send:** nothing in the body — just the product's `id` in the URL, plus the admin bearer token (auto-filled from `{{token}}`).

**Good to know:**
- **Admin-only**: a non-admin token gets `403 Forbidden` (same behavior as Create/Update).
- Deleting an `id` that doesn't exist returns `404 Product not found` rather than a false "success" — useful for catching a stale/already-deleted id on the frontend.
